correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 the chain starts with n labels holding one vote and uses simultaneous n-trial multinomial draws with probabilities proportional to squared current counts. Put m!<=n<(m+1)!; standard occupancy first and second factorial moments uniformly locate the first-round maximum M in m−1,m,m+1 and show its runner-up population S=U_{M−1} exceeds the top-class population R=U_M by at least a constant m/log(m) factor with probability tending to one; both groups together have polynomial-in-m size. Q=sum_i X1_i² satisfies Q/n→2 in probability. Conditional Poisson approximation for the top two occupancy classes has total variation O(m^12/n)=o(1), with means mu=n M²/Q and nu=n(M−1)²/Q. At T=ceil(mu+sqrt(2mu(log R+log(m)/4))), a Chernoff upper bound makes all original leaders fall below T, while an explicit Poisson moderate-deviation lower bound gives S Pr(Poi(nu)>=T)≥m^{3/4−o(1)}→infinity; hence some original runner-up exceeds all previous leaders strictly, including tied leaders. The eventual-winner corollary is mathematically conditional on the source study’s claimed P(W in L2)→1 at the critical exponent; that external premise was not independently verified from the inaccessible complete primary text. Fresh enumeration verified the two-round strict-turnover probabilities 0 (n=2), 26/375 (n=3), 10111/160000 (n=4), not the asymptotic theorem.
